elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly provides that “Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 requires “30 days' prior written notice to MSL.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: MSL must “refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 states that “MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days' prior written notice, which is outside the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the condition for applying the three-month cap is absent.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 bars MSL from terminating for convenience during the initial or any renewal term, while the existing renewal provision permits either party to end the relationship at a term boundary by preventing renewal.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term termination-for-convenience right requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The existing end-of-term provision requires six months' written notice, not 90 days' notice.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day convenience termination right and a pro-rata refund, while MSL is barred from terminating for convenience during committed terms. It does not independently satisfy every fallback element because the operative notice periods are 30 days for Customer and six months for MSL rather than the fallback's 60–90 days and 90 days, respectively. The addition is targeted and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
